config.title: Build bundle size guard script

intro.title: Build bundle size guard script
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a script that checks the size of your JavaScript project's final bundle file to ensure it doesn't exceed a set limit. You'll learn how to use Node.js to read a file from the filesystem and calculate its size in bytes. The core programming concept involves using the built-in 'fs' module for file operations and conditional logic to compare sizes. By the end, you'll have a practical guard script that can be integrated into a build process to prevent large bundles from being deployed.
intro.usecase: In modern web development, monitoring bundle size is critical for performance optimization. This pattern is used in CI/CD pipelines at companies like Netflix and Airbnb to prevent performance regressions before deployment. Developers implement bundle size guards in dashboard build tools, form submission workflows, and e-commerce checkout processes to ensure fast loading times. For example, a shopping cart modal's JavaScript bundle must stay under size limits to maintain smooth user interactions during peak traffic.

objectives: Construct a script that calculates the size of a JavaScript bundle file
Initialize configuration variables for maximum allowed bundle size
Implement file system operations to read and analyze build artifacts
Apply conditional logic to compare actual bundle size against limits
Configure the script to output clear warnings when size thresholds are exceeded
Integrate the guard script into a build process or package.json script
Manipulate file paths and names to target specific build outputs

steps.title: Import Node.js file system and path modules
steps.instruction: Import the Node.js file system (fs) and path modules using require() syntax.
steps.hint: Use require('fs') and require('path') to import these core Node.js modules.
steps.seedCode: // Import the fs and path modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs and path modules are imported and ready to use for file operations.
successCriteria: fs and path modules are imported using require() syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both fs and path modules using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: you need to use require('fs') and require('path') to import these modules.

steps.title: Define the main guard function
steps.instruction: Create a function named checkBundleSize that accepts two parameters: bundlePath and maxSizeKB. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to include both parameters in parentheses.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the fs and path modules here

// Create the checkBundleSize function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named checkBundleSize is defined with two parameters: bundlePath and maxSizeKB.
successCriteria: The checkBundleSize function exists and accepts bundlePath and maxSizeKB as parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named exactly 'checkBundleSize' and accepts both bundlePath and maxSizeKB parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match what's needed. Create a function named checkBundleSize with bundlePath and maxSizeKB as parameters.

steps.title: Initialize file path resolution
steps.instruction: Inside the checkBundleSize function, use path.resolve() to convert the bundlePath parameter to an absolute path and store it in a variable named absoluteBundlePath.
steps.hint: Call path.resolve(bundlePath) and assign the result to a const variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Converting a relative path to absolute
const absolutePath = path.resolve('./my-file.js');
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have an absoluteBundlePath variable containing the resolved absolute path.
successCriteria: The checkBundleSize function contains a const absoluteBundlePath = path.resolve(bundlePath) statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using path.resolve() correctly and storing the result in a variable named absoluteBundlePath.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using path.resolve(bundlePath) to get the absolute path and assign it to a variable named absoluteBundlePath.

steps.title: Handle missing file error
steps.instruction: Inside the checkBundleSize function, after checking if the bundle file exists, throw an Error with a descriptive message if the file doesn't exist.
steps.hint: Use the fs.existsSync method to check if the file exists, then use throw new Error() with a message like 'Bundle file not found'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now properly handle missing bundle files by throwing a descriptive error.
successCriteria: The checkBundleSize function includes an if statement that checks if the file doesn't exist and throws an Error with a descriptive message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the existence check and the error throwing. The error message should clearly indicate what went wrong.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling for missing files isn't implemented correctly. You need to check if the file exists and throw an Error with a descriptive message when it doesn't.

steps.title: Compare with maximum allowed size
steps.instruction: Inside the checkBundleSize function, add an if statement that compares the calculated file size in kilobytes with the maxSizeKB parameter.
steps.hint: Use the variable you calculated in the previous step (sizeKB) and compare it with maxSizeKB using the greater than (>) operator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function now contains conditional logic to compare the actual bundle size with the maximum allowed size.
successCriteria: An if statement compares sizeKB with maxSizeKB using the > operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're comparing sizeKB with maxSizeKB using the > operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The if statement is missing or doesn't properly compare sizeKB with maxSizeKB. Try using: if (sizeKB > maxSizeKB) { ... }

steps.title: Throw error if bundle exceeds limit
steps.instruction: Inside the if statement that compares sizeKB with maxSizeKB, add code to throw an Error when the bundle size exceeds the limit. The error message should include both the actual size and the maximum allowed size.
steps.hint: Use the throw keyword with new Error() to create an error. Include sizeKB and maxSizeKB values in the message string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now throw a descriptive error when the bundle file exceeds the specified size limit, helping developers identify size violations.
successCriteria: An Error is thrown inside the if statement when sizeKB exceeds maxSizeKB, with a message containing both size values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to throw an Error (not just console.log) and include both the actual and maximum sizes in the message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling isn't quite right. Remember to use throw new Error() with a message that shows sizeKB and maxSizeKB values.

steps.title: Add success message for valid bundles
steps.instruction: Add a console.log() statement at the end of your function that outputs a success message when the bundle size is within the allowed limit.
steps.hint: Place the console.log() after the if statement that checks if the bundle exceeds the limit, so it only runs when the bundle is acceptable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now log a confirmation message to the console when the bundle size is within the allowed limit, providing positive feedback.
successCriteria: A console.log() statement is added at the end of the function that outputs a success message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a console.log() statement that outputs a success message at the end of the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The success message hasn't been added correctly. Add a console.log() statement at the end of the function to output a confirmation when the bundle size is acceptable.
